title: alpha_vantage is a named data fallback that does not exist anywhere in the codebase
repro: grep -rn 'alpha_vantage|AlphaVantage|alphavantage' sidecar/ -> 0 hits outside this census's own new files; sidecar/requirements.txt has yfinance==1.3.0 but no alpha_vantage/alphavantage package at all
evidence: sidecar/requirements.txt (no alpha_vantage entry); sidecar/services/provider_registry.py (no alpha_vantage provider registered); docs/BLUEPRINT.md:252 "yfinance + alpha_vantage fallbacks (no API key needed for basic use)"
notes: yfinance is real and wired; alpha_vantage is not a partial implementation, it is entirely absent - no dependency, no provider module, no route. Alpha Vantage also requires a free API key, contradicting the promise's own "no API key needed" framing, so the promise as written was never buildable as stated. Smallest fix: either add a real alpha_vantage provider behind the existing provider_registry fallback chain, or drop the claim from BLUEPRINT.md §4 Data Layer.

title: Portfolio risk analytics (VaR, Beta, correlation matrix) do not exist anywhere; Sharpe/Sortino/Calmar/max-drawdown exist only inside the backtest engine, never for the user's live tracked portfolio
repro: grep -rn 'value_at_risk|\bVaR\b|def.*beta|correlation_matrix' sidecar/services sidecar/routers -> 0 hits anywhere in the whole sidecar. grep -n 'sharpe|sortino|calmar' sidecar/services/*.py -> matches ONLY inside sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py (lines 236-282, 480); sidecar/services/portfolio_db.py and sidecar/models/portfolio.py have no risk-metric fields at all, only cost_basis/quantity
evidence: sidecar/services/backtest_engine.py:236-282 (sharpe/sortino/calmar computed only for a backtest run); sidecar/models/portfolio.py (position model: no risk fields); sidecar/services/portfolio_db.py (no risk computation); docs/BLUEPRINT.md:266 "Risk analytics (Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, VaR, Beta, max drawdown, correlation matrix)" listed under Portfolio & Risk, not Backtesting
notes: 4 of the 7 named metrics exist, but only for a simulated backtest run, not for what the user actually holds - a Portfolio & Risk module promise is being met by a different module (Backtesting) for a subset of metrics. VaR, Beta and a correlation matrix are 0% built anywhere. Not the subject of code-portfolio.json (that file covers data-sync/UI defects in the existing portfolio panel, not missing risk-metric capability). Smallest fix: either compute Sharpe/Sortino/Calmar/maxDD/VaR/Beta/correlation on the live portfolio's return series in portfolio_db.py and surface it in the panel, or correct BLUEPRINT.md to describe risk analytics as backtest-only.

title: No license-gate UI exists; the only place PolyForm/commercial licensing is mentioned to a user is one passive bullet inside a first-launch TOS modal whose subject is now-removed live trading
repro: grep -rln 'LicenseGate|license.*gate|LicenseModal|LicenseDialog' src/ -> 0 hits; grep -n license src/components/OnboardingFlow.tsx src/components/OnboardingBanner.tsx -> 0 hits. The only licensing text anywhere in the UI is src/modules/safety/DisclaimerFlow.tsx:44 (TOS_BODY, one bullet of five), rendered by FirstLaunchTosDialog which is unconditionally mounted at src/app/page.tsx:289 for every new user (DisclaimerFlow.tsx:81-95: title "Welcome to Vysted", description "Please review the operating terms before connecting a broker")
evidence: src/modules/safety/DisclaimerFlow.tsx:35-121 (TOS_BODY + FirstLaunchTosDialog); src/app/page.tsx:19,289 (DisclaimerFlow mounted unconditionally, not gated on broker-connect intent); docs/BLUEPRINT.md:283 "License gate UI (PolyForm Strict/commercial choice on first launch)"; docs/redesign/DECISIONS.md:141 (D81, 23 Sep - trading removed from the product)
notes: Two compounding problems on the same surface: (1) there is no interactive choice between noncommercial and commercial licensing anywhere - a user cannot pick or even meaningfully acknowledge a license, the text is just present in an unrelated dialog; (2) that dialog's own copy ("before connecting a broker", order confirmation, "kill switch halts all order routing") describes a live-trading product D81 explicitly removed on 23 Sep, so the one modal every new user is forced to read on first launch is now largely describing a feature that no longer exists. Smallest fix: split the dialog - rewrite TOS_BODY to drop the order/kill-switch language (or fold it back into the per-broker first-connect ack where it belongs), and add a real first-launch license acknowledgment naming PolyForm Strict 1.0.0 vs the commercial license.

title: "Multi-window" is unbuilt - the app is a single fixed Tauri window; only multi-tab (dockview panels) exists
repro: python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('src-tauri/tauri.conf.json'))['app']['windows'])" -> exactly one window entry ("Vysted Terminal", fixed size/min-size); grep -rln 'popout|pop-out|newWindow|WebviewWindow|secondary window' src/ src-tauri/src/*.rs -> 0 hits anywhere
evidence: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json app.windows (array of 1); src-tauri/src/lib.rs (no WebviewWindowBuilder / additional-window spawn code); docs/BLUEPRINT.md:235 "Multi-window / multi-tab layout"
notes: Multi-tab is real and substantial (dockview panel host, PanelHost.tsx). Multi-window - popping a chart or research brief out to its own OS window, useful on a multi-monitor trading desk, which is exactly this product's stated user - has zero implementation: no second-window spawn path exists in the Rust core or the frontend. Smallest fix: either scope the promise down to "multi-tab only" in BLUEPRINT.md, or add a minimal pop-out-panel-to-window affordance via a second WebviewWindowBuilder call.
